newsitem.title: UK: British Gas North Morecambe field up again.
newsitem.headline: British Gas North Morecambe field up again.

text.p: Gas production at British Gas Plc's North Morecambe field resumed in early October after a four-month shutdown for operational maintenance, a spokesman for British Gas Trading said on Tuesday.
The field is scheduled to be used close to its "maximum availabilty" for the remainder of 1996, the spokesman said.
British Gas opened the taps at the South Morecambe field on September 19, after maintenance there had also halted production since the beginning of June.
Offtake at that field has been scheduled to correspond to the "seasonal profile of demand" the spokesman said.
British Gas declined to give details of current production rates at the fields due to commercial sensitivity.
The total production capacity of the North and South Morecambe fields in the Irish Sea is estimated at 1.9 billion cubic feet per day, or nearly 16 percent of total U.K. gas output.
The wholly-owned fields give British Gas a huge swing capacity which some in the industry claim is open to abuse.
In September, U.K. industry regulator Ofgas said it was looking into rumours that British Gas had deliberately cut production at Morecambe to push spot market prices higher.
"We are looking at this as part of a wide-ranging look at the market," said an Ofgas spokesman on Tuesday. "We are looking to report sometime next year."
